title: Accept 30005118: Cyclic self-sumset recognition: a credited corollary of the integer hardness theorem
body:
## Accepted result and published preprint

**Cyclic self-sumset recognition: a credited corollary of the integer hardness theorem**, Alec Kriebel. Published paper and verification package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23430681 (https://zenodo.org/records/23430681).

Credited exposition of the cyclic consequence of the integer hardness theorem of Abboud, Fischer, Safier, and Wallheimer. Ordinary all-pair self-sumset recognition in the same Z/nZ, with unbounded positive input n, is NP-complete separately for binary n with an explicit binary residue list and for an n-bit characteristic vector. Hardness holds already for odd n and nonempty B containing 0 with every canonical 2b<n. The universal proof gives integer normalization and an odd zero-anchor/no-wrap transfer; dense hardness uses the AFWS uniform 3SAT numerical bound 2^57(v+c)^4. A deterministic polynomial-time exact decision algorithm in either model exists iff P=NP. No new hardness gadget, novelty, first-publication, independent-discovery, or worldwide-openness claim is made. Extensive AI assistance was used in reasoning, source work, adversarial checking, coding, computational verification and writing. Unrefereed; no external human peer review or formal certification. Support includes byte-preserved original records and authored verification code, not third-party source bodies. Inspected AFWS proof: arXiv2410.18661v2 (26 October 2024); SODA2025 publication metadata separately verified.

## Accepted scope and review

Same-group ordinary cyclic self-sumset recognition is NP-complete in both explicit sparse binary and dense bit-vector encodings, already odd n, target zero-anchor and representatives <n/2.

No gap asserted for exact decision languages; unrestricted meanings of efficient, unconditional P!=NP, randomized/approximation/oracle claims excluded.

The result is accepted at the exact audited head `b7e55279707ce2c720304ca98111088d7d037371`. 2 fresh independent complete AI whole-package reviews were completed, with the final review finding zero actionable issues. Subsequent bounded administrative adoption is recorded in the current external ROOT final seal; earlier status/counter/hold fields remain dated history. Prior mathematical results and proof dependencies are credited. Historical novelty and worldwide current openness are unestablished. AI tools were used extensively; this is an unrefereed preprint, without conventional human peer review or formal proof certification.

The repository Zenodo uploader verified the exact reviewed metadata and PDF/support bytes. The Google Workspace CLI recorded the DOI/details in the requested tracker with exact read-back. No GitHub release is created. Current audit and publication receipts: `audits/pr1052_30005118`.

## Conclusion and credit

Add the complete certificate and independent mathematical audit for 30005118 / OWR-10252930-031. Same-group cyclic self-sumset recognition is NP-complete in both explicit sparse binary and dense characteristic-vector encodings, already for odd n and nonempty zero-containing targets below n/2. A polynomial-time algorithm in either model exists if and only if P=NP. This is not an unconditional impossibility claim.

Integer NP-hardness and the bounded-universe construction are credited to Abboud, Fischer, Safier, and Wallheimer, *Recognizing Sumsets is NP-Complete*, [arXiv:2410.18661v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.18661v2), [SODA 2025](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/1.9781611978322.153). The elementary integer-to-cyclic transfer is supplied in full as a source-applicability argument without a novelty claim. No new hardness gadget construction or full independent audit of the source gadgets is asserted.

## Full proof and audit

The restricted nonempty language uses the explicitly permitted fixed YES replacement (3,{0}). The audit retains every substantive source, mathematical and encoding check and all scope limits.

Only computational reproduction sections and obsolete or out-of-edition administrative framing are removed. All certificate proof sections and substantive audit sections are byte-identical to their reviewed originals. The source ledger is unchanged.
